channel.rule: Name "udev" maps to MONITOR_GROUP_UDEV and calls device_monitor_new_full with fd=-1. NULLname mapsNONE; "kernel" mapsKERNEL; unsupportedname returns NULL/EINVAL. No channel substitution proposed.

disable_predicate.effect: Replace requested group2 with group0 while still creating a usable monitor object/socket; this is normal library behavior in unsupported service context, not an enable-receiving error.

exact_behavior.enable_constructor_branch: For the actual "udev" caller, group2 is retained if the control-path F_OK check succeeds OR dev_is_devtmpfs returnspositive. These are constructor heuristics; neither alone proves a running publisher or event delivery.

devtmpfs_definition.rule: Resolve currentnamespace /dev mountID; read /proc/self/mountinfo; locate same mountID and accept filesystem name beginningdevtmpfs. Otherwise0 or negativeerror, both <=0. A private tmpfs /dev does not satisfy it; statfs TMPFS alone is not substituted for this test.

socket.rule: New AF_NETLINK SOCK_RAW|CLOEXEC|NONBLOCK protocol NETLINK_KOBJECT_UEVENT15; bind sockaddr_nl with selectedgroup, enable ordinary sender process-identity metadata, then get kernel-assigned netlinkportID. PortID need not equal daemonPID.

enable_receiving.rule: udev_monitor_enable_receiving aliases filter_update. It updates the socketfilter; it does not change nl_groups, create a missing service or enable a group0 socket.

normal_transport.rule: Processed udev messages use group2 and normal libudev wire framing. Device-monitor sender defaults to groupUDEV. Hardware-event debug context warns that non-main-netns sockets cannot see hardware events; constructor does not enforce or repair that namespace. A control-node bind alone establishes no publisher/event-path association.

lifetime_ABI.rule: Existing opaque pointer public C ABI stays unchanged: new monitor owns one reference, enable/filter returns int0/negative, get_fd returns owned monitor socket int, receive returns an allocateddevice orNULL, unref releases monitor/socket.
